scientific_model.concept: Knowledge Distillation: Soft Targets, Temperature, and the T² Factor
scientific_model.purpose: Explain how a teacher's logits become soft targets via a temperature-scaled softmax, how the soft-target cross-entropy is computed, and why the soft loss is multiplied by T² when combined with a hard-label loss.
scientific_model.focus_alignment: Section 2: explain knowledge distillation with small teacher and student logit vectors and adjustable temperature. Show the soft probability distributions and the soft-target cross-entropy or a clearly labeled component of it. Explain the temperature effect and the T-squared factor when combining soft and hard training losses. Do not train models.

assumptions: Teacher and student logit vectors are fixed small vectors for one transfer example; no training occurs.
The hard-label target is a one-hot distribution over the same classes, and the hard loss uses the student's T=1 softmax.
limitations: Only one transfer example is shown; real distillation averages over a transfer set.
The gradient-scaling argument for T² is stated from the paper but not derived here; we only apply the factor to the loss combination.
misconceptions: That temperature changes the teacher's knowledge or the student's logits themselves. Temperature only rescales the logits inside the softmax, changing the sharpness of the resulting distribution; the underlying logits are unchanged.
edge_cases: T = 1 makes the soft distribution identical to the ordinary softmax, so soft and hard targets use the same temperature.
Very large T drives the soft distribution toward uniform, so the soft cross-entropy approaches entropy of the teacher distribution and carries little class-specific signal.
scientific_model.demonstration_scope: A single transfer example with small teacher and student logit vectors. We compute the temperature-scaled softmax distributions, the soft-target cross-entropy component, and the T²-scaled combination with a hard-label cross-entropy. No model training, no gradient derivation, no multi-example dataset.

lesson_spec.central_learning_question: Explain how a teacher's logits become soft targets via a temperature-scaled softmax, how the soft-target cross-entropy is computed, and why the soft loss is multiplied by T² when combined with a hard-label loss.
learning_objectives: Compute temperature-scaled softmax distributions for teacher and student logits and describe how increasing T softens them.
Compute the soft-target cross-entropy component and the T²-scaled weighted combination with a hard-label cross-entropy.
audience_prerequisites: Softmax as a normalized exponential of logits.
Cross-entropy H(p,q) = -Σ p_i ln q_i in nats.
lesson_spec.intuition: A teacher's raw scores (logits) are turned into a probability distribution by a softmax. Raising the temperature T flattens that distribution, exposing relative similarities between classes that a hard label hides. The student is trained to match this soft distribution. Because the soft-target gradients shrink like 1/T², the soft loss is multiplied by T² so that changing T does not silently change the balance between soft and hard objectives.
teaching_sequence: Change each scientific input and compare the live intermediates.
Apply both exploration setups and explain the difference.

guided_explorations.title: Temperature softens the targets
guided_explorations.change: Set v (teacher logits) to [3.0, 1.0, -1.0]; Set z (student logits) to [2.0, 0.5, -0.5]; Set T to 5.0; Set α (hard-loss weight) to 0.3.
guided_explorations.observe: Calculated results for this setup, compared with the starting inputs: p (teacher soft targets) = [0.47177622, 0.31624106, 0.21198272] (starting value: [0.66524096, 0.24472847, 0.090030573]); q (student soft distribution at T) = [0.42601251, 0.31559783, 0.25838965] (starting value: [0.56854641, 0.26856231, 0.16289128]); H(p, q) soft-target cross-entropy = 1.0541502 nats (starting value: 0.86075689 nats); q₁ (student distribution at T=1) = [0.76615721, 0.17095278, 0.062890013] (starting value: [0.76615721, 0.17095278, 0.062890013]); H(y, q₁) hard-label cross-entropy = 0.2663679 nats (starting value: 0.2663679 nats); L combined loss = 26.433666 nats (starting value: 3.5229379 nats).
guided_explorations.why: Dividing logits by a larger T compresses their differences before the softmax, so the exponential ratios move toward uniform. The soft cross-entropy then reflects a flatter target, and the T² multiplier compensates the 1/T² gradient scaling so the soft objective's relative weight stays comparable.

guided_explorations.title: Hard-loss weight changes the balance
guided_explorations.change: Set v (teacher logits) to [3.0, 1.0, -1.0]; Set z (student logits) to [2.0, 0.5, -0.5]; Set T to 2.0; Set α (hard-loss weight) to 0.8.
guided_explorations.observe: Calculated results for this setup, compared with the starting inputs: p (teacher soft targets) = [0.66524096, 0.24472847, 0.090030573] (starting value: [0.66524096, 0.24472847, 0.090030573]); q (student soft distribution at T) = [0.56854641, 0.26856231, 0.16289128] (starting value: [0.56854641, 0.26856231, 0.16289128]); H(p, q) soft-target cross-entropy = 0.86075689 nats (starting value: 0.86075689 nats); q₁ (student distribution at T=1) = [0.76615721, 0.17095278, 0.062890013] (starting value: [0.76615721, 0.17095278, 0.062890013]); H(y, q₁) hard-label cross-entropy = 0.2663679 nats (starting value: 0.2663679 nats); L combined loss = 3.6561219 nats (starting value: 3.5229379 nats).
guided_explorations.why: The hard weight α multiplies only the hard cross-entropy, so raising α increases the hard objective's contribution without altering the soft-target cross-entropy or the temperature scaling.
